## Method and limitations

This turn was packet-only: no tools, no commands, no dynamic execution. I did not verify the HEAD/base/worktree identity myself (instructed not to call tools); the frozen-identity claim is taken from the orchestrator. I did not read other reviewers' output or the run report. Everything below is derived from the supplied diff and the supplied line-numbered excerpts of `cli/src/native/actions.rs`, `cli/src/native/browser.rs`, `cli/src/native/tab_binding.rs`, `cli/src/connection.rs`.

Source **not** supplied and therefore unverifiable (marked where it matters): `DaemonState::new()`, `skip_launch_action`, `BrowserManager::connect_cdp_isolated` / `connect_auto_isolated`, `dispose_unpersisted_isolated_context`, `mark_isolated_context_persisted`, `context_recreated` mutation points, `binding_snapshot`, the CLI-side construction of the `isolateContext` command field in `main.rs`, and the enclosing function of `browser.rs:589-597`.

## Solution shape

The core repair is right and mostly minimal: the pre-fix code committed `state.isolate_context = true` in the command preamble, before validation, before connection, before persistence. The fix replaces that with (a) threading the *requested* isolation as a parameter (`auto_launch(..., isolate_context)`, `connect_external_cdp/auto(..., isolate_context)`, `handle_launch`'s local `isolate_context` at `actions.rs:4750`), and (b) a single commit point after the response is known (`commit_isolated_connection`, `actions.rs:3303`).

Three of the "extra" lifecycle changes are genuinely required, not gratuitous:

- `apply_tab_binding_on_attach` switching from `state.isolate_context` to the manager's real isolation (`actions.rs:3223-3226, 3261, 3275, 3283`). With deferred commit, `state.isolate_context` is `false` during a first isolated attach, so the old reads would have broken the attach semantics.
- Deferring the binding write for isolated launches (`actions.rs:3049`, `3287`). Because the durable record (`IsolatedBindingV1`, `tab_binding.rs:55-63`) is what makes isolation sticky across daemon restarts, writing it at attach time would durably poison later flagless commands exactly as acceptance item 2 forbids. Deferral is the correct shape here.
- `close_after_network_control_failure` using `rollback_failed_launch` instead of `close_current_browser` (`actions.rs:2398`). Without it, a late network-control failure would leave an orphan `BrowserContext` in the shared Chrome.

The one shape choice I would push back on is the *pair* of failure branches (`3031` and `3104-3111`) with different guards; see F1.

## Findings

**F1 — Medium. Unnecessary teardown of an already-committed isolated session on an unrelated action error.**
`actions.rs:3031`
```
if lifecycle_launched && isolated_launch && result.is_err() { rollback_failed_launch }
```
has no `!state.isolate_context` guard, while its sibling at `3104-3108` does. Trigger: an established sticky isolated session (`state.isolate_context == true`, binding already persisted) whose CDP connection is dead or whose Chrome restarted. Any command then takes `needs_launch == true` (`actions.rs:2660-2664`) → `auto_launch(..., true)` reconnects (`lifecycle_launched = true`, `isolated_launch = true`), and then a perfectly ordinary action error — selector not found, navigation timeout, `net::ERR_*` — fires the rollback. Wrong outcome: `rollback_failed_launch` (`actions.rs:4705`) closes the browser connection and clears webmcp/iframe/screencast/input/ref-map state; and if the context had just been recreated after a Chrome restart, `dispose_unpersisted_isolated_context()` destroys that fresh context and its tab (including anything `try_auto_restore_state` just restored during the same `auto_launch`), because commit never ran to mark it persisted. Nothing about acceptance item 2 requires this: sticky state was already `true`, so there is nothing to avoid enabling. Non-isolated sessions keep their browser in the identical scenario, so this is an isolation-only behavioral asymmetry introduced by the fix.

**F2 — Medium (conditional on unsupplied source). Possible latched `context_recreated` making F1's teardown permanent.**
`actions.rs:3107` consults `manager.context_recreated()` (the manager-level flag, `browser.rs:1473-1475`), not the per-command `state.context_recreated`, which is the only one reset (`actions.rs:3113`). If the manager flag is set once at connect and never cleared for the life of the manager (`mark_isolated_context_persisted` is only documented by name), then after a single Chrome restart every subsequent failing command with `isolated_launch == true` takes the rollback branch even after the new context id was durably committed. I cannot confirm the clearing point from the packet; if the flag is cleared on persist, this finding collapses into F1.

**F3 — Low/Medium. Commit can report success with nothing written to disk.**
`commit_isolated_connection` (`actions.rs:3309`) treats `maybe_persist_tab_binding == None` as "persisted", but that function returns `None` both for "unchanged" and for "no snapshot": `let (target_id, url) = mgr.binding_snapshot()?;` (`actions.rs:3176`) early-returns `None` when the manager has no bindable target (tab_gone / zero pages). In that case `state.isolate_context = true` is committed while the durable isolated binding may never have been written, so a daemon restart silently reverts the session to the shared default context. The pre-fix code had a hard error for this class of failure at attach time; the fix removed `state.isolate_context` from that hard-error condition (`actions.rs:3291`, now `if state.pin_tab`) and moved durability to commit, which does not distinguish the two `None`s.

**F4 — Low. Crash window leaks a `BrowserContext` in the shared browser.**
Between `connect_*_isolated` (context created) and `commit_isolated_connection` (context id recorded), no record of the new context exists anywhere. A daemon kill/panic in that window leaves an orphan context in the host's Chrome that no later daemon will adopt or dispose. Pre-fix, the attach-time write closed this window. This is an accepted cost of the (correct) deferral, but it is a real new state.

**F5 — Low. Commit failure discards the response envelope.**
`actions.rs:3101-3103` replaces `resp` wholesale with `error_response`, dropping `tab_gone` data, the lifecycle block, and any warning already attached at `3059-3085`, and the message ("cannot persist the session isolation binding: …") does not tell the caller that the internal `rollback_failed_launch` also closed the browser and discarded the action's session. Callers that key on lifecycle fields will misread this envelope.

**F6 — Medium, unverified. Removing the daemon env makes isolation depend on every envelope carrying the field.**
`connection.rs:572-575` and `main.rs:1722` delete `AGENT_BROWSER_ISOLATE_CONTEXT` from daemon spawn env. Previously a daemon spawned with `--isolate-context` was isolated regardless of whether a particular command envelope carried `isolateContext`. Now `handle_launch` (`4750`), the implicit-launch call (`2755-2760`), and the guard (`2637`) all read the per-command field. If any CLI code path builds a command envelope without propagating the flag, `--isolate-context` silently degrades to the shared default context — a confidentiality failure strictly worse than the bug being fixed, and one that no supplied test would catch (the tests construct JSON directly, and the two CLI-level tests are `#[ignore]`d). I could not inspect the envelope construction in `main.rs`, so this is a boundary to verify rather than a confirmed defect: `grep` every site that emits `isolateContext` and confirm it covers all subcommand shapes (including `connect <port|url>` and any non-`launch` envelope).

**F7 — Low, unverified. `Browser.setDownloadBehavior` now carries both a page `sessionId` and `browserContextId`.**
`browser.rs` `set_download_behavior` keeps `Some(session_id)` and adds `params["browserContextId"]`. Chrome's `BrowserHandler` attached to a *page* session is restricted, and whether an explicit `browserContextId` resolves there (rather than erroring, or being ignored in favour of the default context) is exactly the property acceptance item 1 depends on. If it is silently ignored, the isolated download reconfigures the *default* context — the original bug, undetected. The only check for this is the `#[ignore]`d `isolated_downloads_preserve_other_context_destinations`. Separately, the second call site (`browser.rs:589-597`, `behavior: "allow"`, no `browserContextId`, `None` session) was not touched; it appears to be on an owned-launch path where the default context is the session's own, but I could not see the enclosing function — confirm it is unreachable for CDP-connected isolated sessions, otherwise a `--download-path` + `--cdp --isolate-context` invocation reconfigures the shared browser.

**F8 — Low. Download event matching remains context-blind.**
`actions.rs:7344-7351` accepts `Browser.downloadWillBegin` / `Browser.downloadProgress` "regardless" of session, by design. Enabling per-context download events on several contexts of one shared Chrome (multiple daemons, each with its own browser websocket) makes cross-talk newly plausible: a foreign `completed` would break the loop early and a foreign GUID would be captured, yielding a spurious "Downloaded file not found at expected path (GUID: …)" (`7403`) or an early success check against the wrong file. Whether Chrome dispatches these to a browser-level session not attached to the originating page is not determinable from the packet. The new concurrent block in the CLI test targets this, but it is `#[ignore]`d and timing-dependent in both directions.

## Boundaries reviewed and found sound

- **Acceptance 2, early returns and invalid modes.** `handle_launch:4767` (isolation without `--cdp/--auto-connect`) and `auto_launch:3945-3952` both reject before any browser exists; the preamble guard (`2637-2648`) no longer mutates state. `skip_launch` actions and policy `deny`/`confirm` return before any launch, so `isolated_launch` is `false` and no commit occurs.
- **Acceptance 2, late fallible stages.** Post-attach failures inside `handle_launch` route through `apply_tab_binding_on_attach_or_rollback`, `install_network_controls_or_close` (now `rollback_failed_launch` via `2401`), and `load_storage_state_or_rollback` (`5027/5045/5067`), all of which drop the browser and dispose the unpersisted context before returning `Err`; `isolated_launch` then evaluates `false` because `state.browser` is `None`, so no commit.
- **Acceptance 2, binding write.** `persisted_browser_context_id` calls `tab_binding::ensure_writable` (`3322`, `tab_binding.rs:199`) *before* connecting, so an unwritable socket dir fails ahead of context creation; the residual save failure is caught in commit and rolled back.
- **Acceptance 3, flag omission and reconnect.** `handle_launch:4750-4751` and `2758-2759` OR the sticky flag with the command field, so a flagless reconnect stays isolated; `isolation_changed` (`4961`) now compares the effective value against `mgr.is_isolated()`, so a flagless launch on an isolated manager does not force a non-isolated relaunch.
- **Acceptance 3, prior success survives later errors.** A failed reconnect (`connect_external_*` error) leaves `state.browser == None` after `close_current_browser` at `4983`, so `isolated_launch` is `false` and neither commit nor rollback touches `state.isolate_context`. Confirmed by inspection, not execution.
- **Acceptance 4, no cross-envelope undo.** With a live connection, a later failing action has `lifecycle_launched == false` and `action != "launch"`, so `isolated_launch == false` and no rollback path is reachable. (The exception is the relaunch-in-the-same-envelope case, F1.)
- **Acceptance 5, recording.** No recording code is touched; the pre-existing isolated-recording e2e is unchanged.
- **Legacy binding compatibility.** `tab_binding::load` (`97-136`) still parses the legacy shape and yields `browser_context_id: None`, which the new `context_changed` check (`3236-3241`) treats as "different context" so a legacy target id is not restored into a new context. This is what makes the pinned→isolated transition land on a fresh target.

## Test weaknesses

1. **Every behavioral test added is `#[ignore]`d except three.** The two `e2e_tests.rs` additions and both `tests/isolate_context_cli.rs` additions require a real Chrome. The default suite gains only `test_isolation_invalid_launch_does_not_change_sticky_state`, `..._skipped_command_...`, `..._policy_rejection_...`.
2. **Those three fast tests are all negative and are satisfied by a strictly broken implementation.** Delete `state.isolate_context = true` from `commit_isolated_connection` entirely — isolation never becomes sticky, acceptance item 3 fully violated — and all three still pass. They assert only "unchanged" and "browser is none". No fast test asserts the positive commit, flag-omission survival, or reconnect.
3. **No fast test covers "connected, then a late stage failed."** In all four rows of test 1, either no browser was ever created or the connect itself failed (`invalid://endpoint`). The rollback-after-successful-connect logic (the actually risky new code at `3031`, `3104-3111`, `3309`) has zero non-ignored coverage.
4. **The `provider: "ios"` row is redundant.** With `isolateContext` and no CDP fields, `handle_launch:4767` fires before any provider handling, so it re-tests row 1's early return, not a provider path.
5. **The `prior = true` half of test 1 is near-vacuous.** Asserting `state.isolate_context == prior` when `prior == true` cannot distinguish "left alone" from "set to true again".
6. **F1's behavior is untested in either suite.** No test asserts that a committed isolated session keeps its browser after a failing action that triggered a relaunch; `failed-reconnect` in the e2e uses a dead port, where the browser is already gone.
7. **The forced-save-failure trick is brittle coupling.** The e2e pre-creates a directory at `…target.tmp.{pid}` to break `tab_binding::save` (`tab_binding.rs:167`). It fails loudly rather than silently if the naming changes, so it is fail-safe, but it encodes a private implementation detail.
8. **The concurrent download block is a timing race.** `thread::scope` with two `download` commands and a 10s polling deadline elsewhere in the same test; a flake here is indistinguishable from the F8 cross-talk it is meant to detect.
9. **Nothing tests F3's "no snapshot" durability hole or F4's crash window.**

## Material unverified assumptions

- `DaemonState::new()` derives `isolate_context` from the persisted isolated binding (and/or the env var), which is the only explanation for `assert!(DaemonState::new().isolate_context)` after commit and `assert!(!DaemonState::new().isolate_context)` after failure/close. If it instead reads only `AGENT_BROWSER_ISOLATE_CONTEXT`, the `connection.rs` env removal would break cross-restart stickiness outright.
- `skip_launch_action("launch") == true` (implied by `(lifecycle_launched || action == "launch")` at `3026`).
- `dispose_unpersisted_isolated_context` is a no-op once `mark_isolated_context_persisted` has been called; this is what bounds F1's damage in the non-recreated case.
- Chrome accepts `Browser.setDownloadBehavior` with a page `sessionId` plus an explicit `browserContextId` (F7).
- All CLI subcommand envelopes propagate `isolateContext` (F6).

## Bottom line

Not defect-free. The commit-on-success restructuring is the right shape and closes the acceptance-2 poisoning cleanly, but the failure side is inconsistent: `actions.rs:3031` lacks the `!state.isolate_context` guard its sibling at `3104` has, so an already-isolated session loses its connection (and, after a Chrome restart, its freshly recreated context) on ordinary action errors (F1/F2). Secondary issues are the "persisted" conflation in commit (F3), the crash-window context leak (F4), and the response-clobbering on commit failure (F5). Two properties central to the acceptance contract — that the flag actually reaches the daemon on every envelope (F6) and that `browserContextId` is honoured on a page session (F7) — are not decidable from source alone and are covered only by ignored tests. The default-suite tests do not reject a "never commit sticky state" implementation and should not be treated as evidence that acceptance item 3 holds.
